ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, individuals with significant control, signatories and authorized agents against the consolidated Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Canadian Criminal Code terrorist list, FINTRAC guidance, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and applicable PEP/adverse-media databases. Screening must be performed before incorporation, again before any disbursement, and periodically thereafter. Positive PEP flags, sanctions hits, or unexplained source-of-funds findings trigger enhanced due diligence and require senior management approval before proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online name reservation and legal name verification portal (Services en ligne du Registraire des entreprises du Québec)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a corporation in Quebec must be in French. It must comply with the Charter of the French Language and the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The name may contain a proper name, a descriptive term in French, and a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée' or 'Fer...' in an accepted French form. English words may appear only as a clearly secondary version to a French legal name. The name must use Latin script; transliteration from non-Latin scripts is not acceptable for registration purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gouvernement du Quebec / Government of Canada

In addition, any name that falsely implies government sponsorship, public institution status, a regulated profession, or a public administrative body is prohibited without the prior written approval of the competent authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal, the Registraire des entreprises du Québec issues a written notice stating the grounds. The applicant may immediately file a corrected or new name application. If the applicant disputes the grounds, it may request an internal administrative review within 30 days of the refusal by submitting written submissions and any corrected legal name. If the internal review confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within 60 days of the review decision. In exceptional urgency, a judicial application for mandamus or judicial review may be filed in the Superior Court of Quebec. All deadlines are strict and require professional legal advice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this low-risk PropTech SaaS business only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec, accepts service of process, forwards mail, and provides work space on demand. A pure post-office box or mail-forwarding-only address is not sufficient. The registered office must be a real and identifiable location in Quebec in which corporate records can be produced and legal process can be served during normal business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first year is below 5% for a standard low-risk registration office and non-licensed SaaS activity. Inspection risk rises if the business shows tax non-compliance, inconsistent filings, suspicious transaction reports, or consumer complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, s. 9-47; if federal incorporation is elected, Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c C-44, s. 5-15. This dossier assumes provincial incorporation in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed through the Registraire's online service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Shares may be issued with or without par value; consideration must be fully paid before issuance. Subscription funds may be held in trust for the corporation prior to constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Articles of Incorporation are hereby appointed the first directors of the corporation; that the subscription agreements for 100 common shares are accepted and the stated consideration is declared adequate; that the registered office of the corporation is established at the address specified in the Articles and that the Quebec Enterprise Registrar is directed to file the same; that the following individuals are appointed officers: Chief Executive Officer and Secretary-Treasurer; and that they are authorized to open bank accounts, enter into agreements, and take all other necessary actions to conclude incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal name search in the Registraire's Central Register for Quebec Enterprises to ensure the proposed name is distinctive, lawful, and not confusing with existing trademarks or corporate names. If the name is acceptable, file a separate declaration and reservation. If a numbered company is preferred, skip this step and proceed with the assigned legal number.
required_dossiers: Proof of compliance with trademark search (internal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name or add distinctive elements; request an administrative review of the refusal within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - 'Services en ligne' portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation form via the online filing service, specifying the share structure (class and number of shares), the first directors, and the registered office address. Submit the document, pay official fees by credit card or electronic funds transfer, and obtain the certificate of constitution once approved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency notice, correct the specified items and re-file; if outright refusal, submit corrected articles or request ministerial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Initial Declaration and Obtain Quebec Enterprise Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the certificate of constitution, file the initial declaration (déclaration initiale) identifying the corporation's registered office, first directors, and officer details. This online filing assigns the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) required for subsequent tax registration and administrative dealings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial declaration is late, file it immediately together with the prescribed late fee and an explanation; if rejected, correct the information and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt By-Laws, Issue Shares, and Complete Organizational Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal corporate action; no government authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first organizational meeting of the board to adopt By-Law No. 1 governing share records, meetings, quorum, and officers; issue share certificates to subscribers against payment; prepare the minutes book, share register, transfer register, and corporate seal if desired.
required_dossiers: Subscription agreements and proof of payment
Share certificate book and corporate registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If formalities are defective, ratify them by a subsequent board resolution and retroactive minute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Federal and Quebec Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via the Combined Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the new business registration online through the Centre de services aux entreprises or CRA Business Registration Online to obtain the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account, GST/HST account, payroll account, and corporate income tax documentation. For a SaaS platform, register for QST on digital services and ensure the service is taxable in Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried or incomplete, contact Revenu Québec or CRA to amend the registration without delay; file all applicable initial tax returns within legislative deadlines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls, mandatory conversion, or routine approval requirements for ordinary commercial receipts and payments. FINTRAC administers anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing compliance for reporting entities, while the Canada Revenue Agency administers tax reporting and withholding rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for current-account and ordinary capital-account transactions. There are no general controls on importing or exporting Canadian dollars, foreign currency, dividends, interest, service fees, royalties, loan proceeds, or sale proceeds. Capital contributions, shareholder loans, acquisitions, and intercompany transfers generally require commercial bank source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership review rather than central-bank approval. Profit remittances are generally permitted after corporate solvency, corporate-law, tax, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, sanctions, and contractual restrictions are satisfied. Dividends must be declared in accordance with the applicable federal or Quebec corporate statute and must not be paid when the corporation is insolvent or unable to meet statutory solvency tests. Payments to non-residents may attract Canadian withholding tax, generally 25 percent under domestic law unless reduced by an applicable treaty, including the Canada-U.S. treaty. Related-party payments require arm's-length support, transfer-pricing records, and applicable Canadian information returns. Quebec tax, French-language documentation, and provincial consumer or privacy obligations may also affect banking and payment operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory repatriation deadline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Canada. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds in Canadian or offshore accounts, subject to contractual banking requirements, sanctions, tax reporting, anti-money-laundering controls, and accurate books and records. Foreign-currency balances and cross-border accounts may be reportable under CRA, Statistics Canada, or other applicable information regimes depending on the account, ownership, transaction, and reporting threshold. The corporation should document the commercial purpose, counterparty, invoice, delivery evidence, and beneficial owner for material cross-border receipts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and operating liquidity; low as a replacement for a primary Canadian corporate bank. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide multi-currency wallets, foreign-exchange conversion, card acquiring, or payment collection only within the scope of its home-jurisdiction authorization and contractual permissions. It may not represent itself as a Canadian deposit-taking institution or accept deposits in Canada without the required Canadian authorization. Funds may be safeguarded rather than insured deposits, and Canadian deposit insurance generally does not apply to offshore EMI balances. Canadian banks, payment processors, Stripe, and ACH providers may require a Canadian operating account, Canadian entity verification, Canadian beneficial-owner information, and transparent settlement flows. The entity must assess Payment Services Act registration requirements where applicable, Quebec consumer and privacy requirements, sanctions screening, PCI DSS, data-residency and outsourcing terms, chargeback exposure, reserve requirements, account-freeze rights, and insolvency segregation risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by every director is not generally mandated by Canadian corporate law. Major banks may permit remote or video onboarding for Canadian-resident corporations, but requirements are discretionary and commonly depend on incorporation jurisdiction, ownership complexity, director residence, business activity, expected transaction volume, source of funds, and country risk. A director, signing officer, or authorized representative may be required to attend an interview or branch appointment. Quebec banks and counterparties may require French-language notices or documentation where legally applicable. Non-resident directors and foreign beneficial owners should expect enhanced verification, notarized or certified identification, proof of residential address, live-video verification, and possible in-person attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, bearer-like ownership arrangements, or inconsistent corporate registries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current federal or Quebec certificate of incorporation, articles and amendments, corporate profile report, registers of directors and individuals with significant control, ownership chart through all entities to natural persons, shareholder register, certified identification, residential-address evidence, and signed beneficial-ownership certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors, shareholders, controllers, or source jurisdictions classified as higher risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passports and secondary identification, proof of address, tax-residency information, professional references, sanctions and politically exposed person screening results, organizational chart, explanation of the Canadian commercial nexus, and evidence of legitimate source and expected destination of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained initial capital injection, shareholder loan, or rapid movement of funds after account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreement, board and shareholder resolutions, capitalization table, investor identity documents, audited or bank-generated source-of-funds evidence, originating-account statements, wire confirmation, purpose narrative, and reconciliation linking each incoming payment to the ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech platform payments that combine subscriptions, tenant-related funds, rental proceeds, security deposits, or third-party money
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed funds-flow map, customer terms, merchant-of-record analysis, platform and property-management agreements, segregation and trust-account analysis, refund and chargeback procedures, payment-processor contracts, invoices, sample transaction files, and confirmation that the company is not conducting unlicensed deposit-taking, remittance, trust, brokerage, or real-estate activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated SaaS activity and transaction profile, including high-value real-estate payments or unrelated international counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, website and product demonstration, NAICS and ISIC classification, customer and vendor lists, signed contracts, invoices, expected monthly volumes, countries and currencies, transaction-flow schedule, tax registrations, and management explanation of exceptional transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, virtual offices, mailbox addresses, unrelated third-party payors, or opaque payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or serviced-office agreement, utility or municipal address evidence, formal corporate payment policy, authorized-signatory matrix, customer-payor relationship evidence, processor agreements, and written prohibition of personal-account use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, cyber-risk, or high-risk-country match
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution memorandum, independent screening results, court or regulatory records, legal opinion where appropriate, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, beneficial-owner confirmation, transaction-specific commercial evidence, and documented escalation and approval decision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate tax, privacy, cybersecurity, or regulatory documentation for a software platform processing personal and financial information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA and Revenu Quebec registrations where applicable, GST/HST and QST analysis, privacy policy, Quebec Law 25 compliance records where applicable, data-processing agreements, cybersecurity controls, incident-response plan, PCI DSS evidence where applicable, insurance certificates, and vendor risk assessments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained foreign exchange losses, excessive cash activity, or frequent transfers between related entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy, approved counterparty list, intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing support, cash forecast, bank reconciliations, FX confirmations, accounting entries, management approvals, and documented business rationale for each material transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian corporate operating or designated capital account by wire transfer from the investor's account to the corporation's account. Use the corporation's exact legal name, account number, institution and transit details, SWIFT/BIC where applicable, and a payment narrative identifying equity subscription, shareholder loan, or other legally accurate purpose. Canada generally does not impose central-bank purpose codes or pre-clearance for inbound capital. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription agreement or loan agreement, board approval, cap table, beneficial-ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, originating bank details, and expected amount and currency. Reconcile the wire to the general ledger and issue shares or record debt only under executed documents. Avoid third-party funding unless fully documented. Screen investors, originating banks, intermediaries, and jurisdictions against applicable Canadian sanctions and AML requirements. Consider withholding tax, thin-capitalization, interest deductibility, transfer-pricing, foreign-affiliate, and shareholder-loan consequences before classifying funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary supplier and service payments, use Canadian domestic EFT, wire, or an approved payment processor; use SWIFT MT103 where supported for cross-border customer or vendor wires, recognizing that ISO 20022 payment messages such as pacs.008 are increasingly replacing legacy SWIFT formats. Retain invoice, purchase order, contract, delivery or acceptance evidence, beneficiary ownership details, sanctions screening, and payment approval. Use commercial documentary letters of credit for higher-risk or document-intensive trade; the issuing bank, confirming bank, and negotiating bank should apply the agreed UCP 600 terms, and electronic presentation should be addressed where applicable. Use bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only after reviewing contingent-liability, collateral, covenant, and fee consequences. ACH Direct is appropriate only for supported Canadian or U.S. account structures and authorized debit mandates; it is not a universal substitute for international wires. For recurring SaaS collections, use Stripe Billing or an equivalent licensed processor with documented merchant-of-record status, settlement account, reserve, chargeback, refund, and customer-verification terms. Apply dual approval, beneficiary-change callbacks, sanctions screening, payment limits, and daily bank reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or regulated dealer to hedge identifiable Canadian-dollar, U.S.-dollar, euro, or other currency receivables and payables. Document notional, maturity, rate, settlement method, underlying exposure, counterparty credit terms, collateral or credit-support requirements, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility or settlement constraints, provided the transaction is entered into with an authorized and appropriately regulated dealer, references a transparent fixing, is connected to a documented commercial exposure, and complies with applicable derivatives, sanctions, reporting, suitability, and collateral requirements.

Cross-currency swaps or interest-rate and currency swaps for material, recurring, or longer-term funding exposures. Obtain board approval, ISDA documentation, eligible-counterparty analysis, netting and close-out review, valuation procedures, collateral terms, liquidity stress testing, and accounting designation before execution.

FX options, collars, and participating forwards may be used for asymmetric or uncertain exposures, subject to suitability, premium, maximum-loss, liquidity, valuation, and hedge-accounting review. Avoid speculative trading and maintain a written treasury policy limiting derivatives to risk-management purposes.

Spot FX conversions through Canadian banks, regulated dealers, or compliant payment providers for ordinary settlement needs. Maintain an approved counterparty list and review Canadian derivatives reporting, trade-repository, margin, business-conduct, and Quebec derivatives-law requirements where the product, counterparty, or transaction falls within their scope.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return and Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuance; applicable only to a federal corporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing filings may result in non-compliant status, monetary penalties for statutory offences, and administrative dissolution after persistent non-compliance, generally following failure to file required annual returns for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration and Annual Registration Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within six months after the end of the corporation's financial year; the annual registration fee is payable in accordance with the applicable annual assessment notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may generate penalties and interest; failure to file or pay may lead to default status, suspension of registration, revocation of registration, or administrative cancellation after notices and statutory procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end; any balance of tax is generally payable two months after year-end, subject to the applicable small-business corporation rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, instalment interest, reassessments, collection enforcement, and potential loss of applicable tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end, subject to Quebec tax administration rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, instalment interest, reassessments, and collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Shareholder Approval or Waiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and corporate records; filed with a regulator only where specifically required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepare and present financial statements at the annual meeting or obtain the applicable shareholder approval or waiver within the statutory period following the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate-law non-compliance, director and officer exposure, shareholder remedies, and potential adverse consequences in tax, financing, diligence, or regulatory reviews.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary private Quebec corporation generally has no automatic audit requirement based solely on revenue, assets, or employee thresholds. An auditor may be required under the applicable federal or Quebec corporate statute, the corporation's articles or by-laws, shareholder rights, financing arrangements, regulated-entity rules, or public-accountability status. Eligible private corporations may generally waive appointment of an auditor through the required shareholder resolution, subject to the governing statute.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for a private corporation; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises and may be adopted where permitted. Tax returns use Canadian federal and Quebec tax rules rather than financial-reporting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain the Register of Members, securities records, and beneficial ownership information continuously. Record share transfers and changes in control promptly. A Quebec corporation must update applicable beneficial ownership information through its annual updating declaration and generally report changes to the Registraire des entreprises within the prescribed change-reporting period. A federal corporation must maintain its ISC register, file required ISC information with Corporations Canada with the annual return, and update the register within 15 days after becoming aware of a change. The annual confirmation does not replace prompt reporting of interim changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Individuals with Significant Control or Beneficial Ownership Register
Articles, By-laws, Shareholder Resolutions, and Annual Filings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_government_renewal_fees: Approximately USD 65 for a Quebec corporation's annual registration fee or approximately USD 8 for a federal corporation's online annual return, excluding tax filings; exact CAD fees and exchange rates control.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 500-1,500 annually for a professional registered-office, records-office, or corporate-secretarial service. Neither Quebec nor federal incorporation generally requires a separate commercial registered agent where the corporation maintains a compliant Canadian registered office and records arrangement.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-12,000 for a small private-company compilation or review engagement; approximately USD 8,000-25,000 or more for an independent audit, depending on transactions, revenue, controls, subsidiaries, and reporting requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (15% rate on first $500,000 taxable income); Quebec SR&ED tax credits; manufacturing and processing tax credit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (CRA My Business portal); Quebec TP-1 Corporate Tax Return (Revenu Québec My Account)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for calendar year-end 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations report solely Canadian-source income; attach T2125 Statement of Business or Professional Activities if applicable
Non-residents include only Quebec-source income; attach supporting schedules for foreign-source adjustments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: $50 per day up to $5,000; Quebec: equivalent daily penalties plus 5% monthly interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 with beneficial ownership certificate, TRC application, and supporting ownership documentation to CRA for DTA relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-15% under applicable treaties (e.g., 0% under US-Canada treaty for substantial holdings); Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million related-party transactions for local file; CAD 50 million consolidated group revenue for master file
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No full Economic Substance Regulations; compliance enforced through GAAR, transfer pricing adjustments, and CFC rules requiring genuine economic activity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false statements, or fictitious deductions in tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $100,000 per count; imprisonment up to 2 years conviction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for corporate tax debts; potential criminal charges, disqualification from office, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission or delayed filing of corporate tax returns beyond statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of $50 per day (federal) capped at $5,000; Quebec equivalent daily surcharges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several personal liability for penalties; directors may face prosecution for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining entities lacking business purpose or real economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under GAAR; full disallowance of deductions and penalties up to 10% of underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil may be pierced; directors exposed to civil restitution claims, imprisonment, and disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain arm's length TP documentation or apply approved methodologies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustments; penalties up to 10% of underpaid tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally accountable for willful TP violations; potential criminal liability
